facts.statement: Minqaria is a genus of lambeosaurine dinosaurs that lived in the Late Cretaceous of Morocco.
facts.quote: Minqaria (meaning "beak") is a genus of lambeosaurine dinosaurs from the Late Cretaceous (Maastrichtian) Ouled Abdoun Basin of Morocco.

facts.statement: The genus Minqaria contains only one known species, Minqaria bata, which is known from a partial skull.
facts.quote: The genus contains a single species, Minqaria bata, known from a partial skull.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen MHNM.KHG.1395 was discovered in the Sidi Chennane locality of the Oulad Abdoun Basin in Morocco.
facts.quote: The Minqaria holotype specimen, MHNM.KHG.1395, was discovered in sediments of the Oulad Abdoun Basin (upper Couche III, Sidi Chennane locality) of Morocco.

facts.statement: Longrich and colleagues described Minqaria bata as a new genus and species in 2024.
facts.quote: In 2024, Longrich et al. described Minqaria bata as a new genus and species of arenysaurin hadrosaurid based on these fossil remains.

facts.statement: The fossil specimen includes a partial skull with a right maxilla, left dentary, and braincase.
facts.quote: The specimen consists of a partial skull, including a right maxilla, left dentary, and braincase.

facts.statement: Minqaria is estimated to have been about 3.5 meters long and weighed 250 kilograms.
facts.quote: Minqaria is estimated to have a length of about 3.5 m and a weight of 250 kg, similar in size to its contemporary relative Ajnabia.

facts.statement: The fused braincase bones suggest the holotype specimen was mature despite its small size.
facts.quote: Since the braincase bones are fused, the Minqaria holotype likely belonged to a mature specimen despite its small size.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis places Minqaria within the hadrosaurid clade Arenysaurini alongside Ajnabia and other Moroccan lambeosaurines.
facts.quote: Longrich et al. (2024) placed Minqaria in a phylogenetic analysis and found it to belong to the hadrosaurid clade Arenysaurini in a clade containing Ajnabia, also known from the Ouled Abdoun Basin, and other Moroccan lambeosaurines

facts.statement: Minqaria lived in the Late Maastrichtian, approximately one million years before the K-Pg extinction event.
facts.quote: These dinosaurs would have lived in the very latest Cretaceous (Late Maastrichtian) approximately 1 million years before the K-Pg boundary and the Chicxulub asteroid impact that wiped out the dinosaurs.

facts.statement: Minqaria fossils were found in nearshore marine phosphate deposits in north-central Morocco.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen was recovered from the phosphates of the Ouled Abdoun Basin of north-central Morocco. The phosphates are a nearshore marine environment dominated by sharks, fish, mosasaurs, and other marine reptiles.

facts.statement: Fossil evidence suggests hadrosaurs were diverse and abundant in the Late Cretaceous Moroccan ecosystem.
facts.quote: Moroccan lambeosaurine fossils belonging to individuals of various sizes, including the holotype of Minqaria, indicate that hadrosaurs were diverse and abundant within the ecosystem.

facts.statement: Researchers consider oceanic dispersal the only viable explanation for how hadrosaurs like Minqaria reached Africa from Europe.
facts.quote: Given this taxonomic position and reconstructions of Late Cretaceous continents and seas, oceanic dispersal between Europe and North Africa is considered the only viable explanation for the presence of hadrosaurs like Minqaria and Ajnabia in Africa.

facts.statement: It remains debated whether intermittent land connections could have facilitated the dispersal of hadrosaurs to Africa alongside oceanic dispersal.
facts.quote: While oceanic dispersal has been considered for the distribution of European hadrosaurs, intermittent land connections as a means of dispersal can not be ruled out.

facts.statement: Hypotheses for dispersal include swimming, drifting, or rafting, though rafting is considered unlikely for large adults but possible for juveniles.
facts.quote: Possible means of dispersal include swimming, drifting, or rafting (wherein animals are transported on top of floating debris or vegetation). Rafting is considered unlikely for a large animal, but it may be possible that young hadrosaurs could be transported this way.

facts.statement: Minqaria is classified within the family Hadrosauridae, subfamily Lambeosaurinae, and tribe Arenysaurini.
facts.quote: familia: Hadrosauridae subfamilia: Lambeosaurinae tribus: Arenysaurini

facts.statement: Minqaria bata lived in Africa during the Late Cretaceous, approximately 68 to 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Minqaria bata (del árabe "pico de pato") es la única especie conocida del género extinto Minqaria, un dinosaurio ornitópodo hadrosáurido que vivió a finales del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente entre 68 a 66 millones de años, durante el Maastrichtiense, en lo que es hoy África.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen MHNM.KHG.1395 was found in sediments of the Oulad Abdoun Basin at the Sidi Chennane locality in Morocco.
facts.quote: El espécimen holotipo de Minqaria, MHNM. KHG.1395, fue descubierto en sedimentos de la cuenca de Oulad Abdoun (superior Couche III, localidad de Sidi Chennane) de Marruecos.

facts.statement: The specimen consists of a partial skull including a right maxilla, left dentary, and a braincase mold.
facts.quote: El espécimen consta de un cráneo parcial, que incluye un maxilar derecho, un dentario izquierdo y un molde del cráneo.

facts.statement: Fossils of Moroccan lambeosaurines of various sizes, including Minqaria, indicate that hadrosaurs were diverse and abundant in the local ecosystem.
facts.quote: Los fósiles de lambeosaurinos marroquíes pertenecientes a individuos de diversos tamaños, incluido el holotipo de Minqaria, indican que los hadrosaurios eran diversos y abundantes dentro del ecosistema.

facts.statement: Minqaria lived during the Maastrichtian stage, from 72.2 to 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Maastrichtian to Maastrichtian (72.2 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: Only one fossil occurrence of Minqaria has been recorded in the scientific database.
facts.quote: Fossil occurrences recorded: 1

facts.statement: Minqaria belongs to the subfamily Arenysaurini.
facts.quote: Parent group: Arenysaurini

facts.statement: Minqaria is classified within the duck-billed dinosaur family Hadrosauridae.
facts.quote: Family: Hadrosauridae

facts.statement: Minqaria is a member of the bird-hipped dinosaur class Ornithischia.
facts.quote: Class: Ornithischia

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Minqaria is Minqaria bata.
facts.quote: Type species: Minqaria bata

facts.statement: During the Late Cretaceous, Minqaria coexisted with its close relative Ajnabia, the predator Chenanisaurus, and sauropods.
facts.quote: Durante el Cretácico tardío, Minqaria coexistió con su pariente cercano Ajnabia junto con el depredador Chenanisaurus y saurópodos.

facts.statement: Oceanic dispersal between Europe and North Africa is considered the only viable explanation for the presence of hadrosaurs like Minqaria in Africa.
facts.quote: La dispersión oceánica entre Europa y el norte de África se considera la única explicación viable para la presencia de hadrosaurios como Minqaria y Ajnabia en África.

facts.statement: It is debated whether intermittent land connections could have served as a dispersal method for Minqaria, though oceanic dispersal is preferred.
facts.quote: no se pueden descartar conexiones terrestres intermitentes como medio de dispersión.

facts.statement: Possible dispersal methods for Minqaria include swimming, drifting, or rafting on floating debris or vegetation.
facts.quote: Los posibles medios de dispersión incluyen nadar, ir a la deriva o hacer rafting (donde los animales son transportados sobre escombros o vegetación flotantes).

facts.statement: While rafting is considered unlikely for a large animal like Minqaria, it is possible that young hadrosaurs could have been transported this way.
facts.quote: El rafting se considera poco probable para un animal grande, pero es posible que los hadrosaurios jóvenes puedan ser transportados de esta manera.

facts.statement: While Laurasia was characterized by tyrannosaurs and ceratopsians, Gondwana was dominated by titanosaurians and abelisaurians, as seen in Morocco.
facts.quote: Mientras que Laurasia se caracteriza por tiranosáuridos y celurosaurios herbívoros, Gondwana está dominada por titanosaurios y abelisaurios, como se ve en Marruecos.

facts.statement: Morocco may have been an isolated island during the time Minqaria lived.
facts.quote: El propio Marruecos puede haber sido una isla aislada.
